title: PayPilot's next growth bet
prompt: PayPilot provides payment software to 12,000 small and midsize merchants in the United States. Growth has slowed, and management can fund only one major initiative next year: cross-sell a new cash-flow forecasting module to current merchants or launch the core payments product in a neighboring country. Management wants to choose the option with the stronger first-year incremental profit and a credible path to durable growth.
objective: Compare cross-selling the forecasting module with geographic expansion and recommend the stronger growth initiative based on first-year incremental profit, strategic fit, and execution risk.

clarificationOptions.label: What metric should drive the decision?
clarificationOptions.response: Prioritize first-year incremental profit, then consider whether the economics and risks can support durable growth.

clarificationOptions.label: Can PayPilot pursue both options?
clarificationOptions.response: No. Product and commercial capacity allow one major initiative next year.

clarificationOptions.label: Which customers are in scope for cross-sell?
clarificationOptions.response: The module is relevant to established merchants with sufficient transaction history, not every current customer.

clarificationOptions.label: Is management considering a brand refresh?
clarificationOptions.response: Brand design is not part of this decision and has no known effect on the two initiatives.

facts.text: 8,000 of PayPilot's 12,000 current merchants have enough transaction history to use the forecasting module.
Research and a paid pilot indicate that 25% of eligible merchants would buy the module at the planned offer.
Each module subscriber would generate $1,200 of annual revenue and $300 of annual variable service cost, or $900 of annual contribution profit.
Cross-selling the module would generate $1.8 million of annual contribution profit before launch cost.
Completing the module and enabling sales would require $600,000 of first-year fixed investment.
The cross-sell initiative would produce approximately $1.2 million of first-year incremental profit after launch investment.
Module customers in the pilot retained at a rate four percentage points above comparable payments-only merchants.
The neighboring country has 30,000 target merchants, but channel and eligibility constraints make 6,000 realistically reachable in year one.
At expected sales productivity, PayPilot could win 1,500 merchants in the new geography during year one.
Each new-country merchant would generate $1,200 of annual revenue and $500 of variable service and support cost, or $700 of contribution profit.
Localization, compliance, and market-entry staffing would require $1.4 million of first-year fixed investment.
Geographic expansion would lose approximately $350,000 in year one before any later scale benefits.
Two established local competitors serve about 60% of the reachable merchants, increasing acquisition uncertainty.
Local regulators permit PayPilot's existing product name and visual identity without modification.

investigationNodes.label: Assess the current customer base
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: PayPilot has 12,000 merchants, including 8,000 with enough transaction history to use the module. The installed-base exhibit is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Estimate module adoption
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: A paid pilot and follow-up research support a 25% conversion rate among eligible merchants.

investigationNodes.label: Evaluate cross-sell economics
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: The module contributes $900 annually per subscriber and requires $600,000 of first-year launch investment. You can now calculate total annual contribution profit.

investigationNodes.label: Check broader customer impact
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Pilot module users retained four percentage points better than comparable payments-only merchants, suggesting a benefit beyond direct profit.

investigationNodes.label: Size the reachable new market
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Although 30,000 merchants fit the broad segment, only 6,000 are realistically reachable in year one. The market funnel is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Estimate first-year merchant wins
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Based on sales capacity and expected conversion, PayPilot could win about 1,500 merchants in year one.

investigationNodes.label: Evaluate expansion economics
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: New-country merchants contribute $700 each, while entry requires $1.4 million of fixed investment. The initiative would lose about $350,000 in year one.

investigationNodes.label: Assess local competition
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Two established competitors already serve roughly 60% of reachable merchants, making the win forecast less certain.

investigationNodes.label: Check local branding requirements
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Regulators allow the existing name and visual identity, so rebranding is unnecessary and immaterial to the decision.

investigationNodes.label: Compare first-year profit and risk
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Cross-sell offers about $1.2 million of first-year incremental profit, while geographic expansion loses about $350,000 and carries greater acquisition uncertainty.

insights.label: A large qualified installed base creates a meaningful cross-sell opportunity.
Every current merchant is expected to purchase the module.
The realistically reachable market is much smaller than the headline segment.
PayPilot can compete for all 30,000 target merchants during year one.
Cross-sell produces $1.55 million more first-year incremental profit than expansion.
Geographic expansion has the stronger first-year profit profile.

calculations.prompt: PayPilot has 8,000 eligible merchants, expects 25% module adoption, and earns $900 of annual contribution profit per subscriber. What annual contribution profit would the cross-sell generate before launch investment?

decisions.label: Prioritize the forecasting-module cross-sell and defer geographic expansion until its entry economics improve.
Enter the neighboring country immediately and defer the module.
Launch both initiatives at full scale next year.

risks.label: Module adoption may fall below the pilot-supported 25% forecast.
Product delays could reduce the module's first-year selling window.
Deferring expansion could allow local competitors to strengthen their positions.

nextSteps.label: Launch to a measured merchant cohort, track adoption and contribution profit, then scale the offer.
Commit immediately to a full new-country office and staffing plan.
Redesign PayPilot's brand before testing either initiative.

efficientPaths.label: Test expansion feasibility, then compare the installed base
